result.reason: The redline does not reach either playbook position. It preserves the existing mutual successor-assignment carveout, so Vendor may assign to a non-competitor successor without Customer consent, contrary to the preferred position. It also allows assignment to a Customer competitor with consent rather than prohibiting it entirely. The fallback is not met because successor assignments require no written notice. In addition, the new Corio carveout conflicts with the retained competitor restriction, and “in whole or in part” unnecessarily expands the permitted assignment right. Unrelated provisions are otherwise preserved, but the operative language is duplicative and ambiguous.
